subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC / integration plan - FastRetail
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Parsons <emma@fastretail.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed PoC / integration plan - FastRetail

Hi Emma + Liam,

Thanks again for your time today — really helpful to get a sense of FastRetail's immediate goals and constraints. Below is a concise recap from our call and a proposed PoC / integration plan so we can align on next steps.

TL;DR (what you said):
- Pain points: slow search/response time on product QA across large catalogs, high per-request cost on current embedding pipeline, and difficulty reproducing inference latencies in production.
- Current stack: internal Node.js service that calls an embedding provider + Redis for vector store; front-end is React; primary infra in us-west-2.
- Success criteria for PoC:
  - 50% reduction in per-query cost for semantic search compared to current provider,
  - median query latency < 120 ms at 95th percentile,
  - end-to-end integration with their existing Node.js backend without schema changes.

Proposed PoC & Milestones (4-week plan):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access + integration checklist completed (owners: Ben/Cust IT).
- Week 1: SDK integration (Node.js) + basic API calls + embedding inference running against a sample dataset (owner: Liam + Ben).
- Week 2: End-to-end pipeline test (embedding -> vector store -> semantic search) with 10k sample queries; collect cost/latency metrics (owner: FastRetail eng + Redwood eng).
- Week 3: Performance tuning (batching, KV caching, quantization suggestions) and ACL/secret handling review (owner: Redwood infra).
- Week 4: Final evaluation vs success criteria, recommendations, and go/no-go decision.

Integration specifics we discussed:
- SDK language: primary PoC in Node.js (we'll provide the Node SDK snippet), Python bindings available if you want to parallelize evaluation.
- API compatibility: Redwood supports streaming completions + batched embedding endpoints. We recommend using our batched embeddings endpoint to reduce per-call overhead.
- Security: Private API keys, optional VPC connector for Dedicated/Private if needed; SOC 2 controls available upon request.

Open questions / assumptions:
- You mentioned the vector store is RedisVector; confirm version and whether you can add an index for the PoC.
- Expected daily query volume during PoC: ~5k queries/day?
- Any strict IP allowlist or network restrictions we need to know about for the kickoff.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Please confirm the PoC timeline above and the engineering owner (Liam?) — reply to confirm.
2) I'll send the Node SDK snippet and a short integration checklist (attached).
3) Schedule the kickoff call (I added a Calendly link below; we can also do Tues/Wed next week).

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (PoC plan & milestones), integration-checklist.csv (access + env vars checklist).

Calendly: https://calendly.com/ben-carter/fastretail-poc
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/3789

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---

Ben — thanks for the thoughtful recap and the clear milestones. Quick confirmations and a couple notes: 

- Yes, pain points captured correctly. Our priority is to validate latency and cost before committing to a vendor switch.
- Stack: RedisVector is v1.6 (self-hosted on an EC2 instance); we can add an index for PoC but will need a maintenance window (Liam to coordinate).
- Estimated PoC traffic: closer to 6k queries/day (not 5k) — mostly read-heavy, with peak times during catalog updates.

A few asks:
- Can you share the Node SDK snippet and an example of batched embedding calls?
- We need recommended settings for batching size and expected memory footprint during peak loads.

Kickoff: Tue 2026-11-10 at 10:00 AM PT works for us — I've tentatively accepted the Calendly invite.

Thanks,
Emma Parsons
Director, Search & Personalization | FastRetail
emma@fastretail.com

Emma — great, thanks for confirming and for the tentative kickoff slot. A couple quick follow-ups before Tue: \

- Node SDK: see snippet below for batched embeddings (also attached in the repo link). We recommend batch sizes of 32–64 for your latency targets; we'll run a tuning pass during Week 3.

Sample Node.js snippet:
```js
// pseudocode snippet
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
const embeddings = await client.embeddings.batch({
  model: 'redwood-embed-v1',
  inputs: chunkedInputs, // array of strings (batch size 32)
});
```

- Memory footprint: for batch size 64 and sequence length ~512 tokens, expect ~10–12GB GPU memory per worker on our quantized profiles; we'll confirm exact numbers on kickoff.
- Network: please confirm if you need an IP allowlist for our hosted endpoints or if you prefer a short-lived API key + proxy through your VPC.

I'll send the meeting invite (Tue 11/10 10:00 AM PT) with agenda and a short demo link. Looking forward to it.

Best,
Ben
